title: Fuel prices going down for third straight week on November 24
summary: Motorists get another round of relief as recovering supplies of global oil and weaker demand lead fuel prices to fall

blocks.text: REFUELING. Motorists queue at a gas station in Paco, Manila, to take advantage of a rollback in gasoline prices, October 20, 2026.
Motorists get another round of relief as recovering supplies of global oil and weaker demand lead fuel prices to fall

MANILA, Philippines – Fuel prices are going down for a third consecutive week starting Tuesday, November 24, as international oil prices continue to decline amid expectations of improving global supplies.
The Department of Energy (DOE) announced the following minimum price decreases for November 24 to 30:

items: Gasoline – rollback of at least P3 per liter
Diesel – rollback of at least P2.60 per liter
Kerosene – rollback of at least P1.60 per liter

blocks.text: The adjustments follow last week’s reductions of P1.50 per liter for gasoline, P3.80 for diesel, and P5.80 for kerosene. Prior to that, gasoline prices plunged by P16.80 per liter, alongside rollbacks of P4.10 for diesel and P3.70 for kerosene.
This comes as global oil markets anticipate a supply surplus, with oil exports from the Middle East recovering and businesses and consumers cutting back on consumption.
However, the continuing US war on Iran and attacks on commercial vessels around the Strait of Hormuz remain risks to global supply.

Despite the recent rollbacks, local pump prices remain substantially higher than before the US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28. In the last full week before the conflict, common Metro Manila prices stood at around P54 to P56 for gasoline, P55 for diesel, and P83.47 for kerosene.
The Philippines imports much of its petroleum requirements as finished products, making domestic prices vulnerable to changes in regional fuel markets, freight costs, and foreign exchange rates.

Excise taxes on liquefied petroleum gas and kerosene have been suspended since late September, under Executive Order No. 125 issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The relief does not cover gasoline or diesel. – Rappler.com
